verses.text: Once again the LORD was angry with Israel, and he stirred up David against them. He said to David, "Go and count the people of Israel and Judah."
So the king said to Joab, the commander of the army who was with him, "Go through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and count the people, so that I will know how many there are."
But Joab said to the king, "May the LORD your God make the people a hundred times more than there are now, and may my lord the king live to see it. But why does my lord the king want to do this?"
But the king's order was stronger than the objections of Joab and the army commanders. So Joab and the commanders left the king and went out to count the people of Israel.
They crossed the Jordan River and camped near Aroer, south of the town in the middle of the valley of Gad. Then they went on to Jazer.
Then they went to Gilead and the land of Tahtim Hodshi, and on to Dan Jaan and around toward Sidon.
They went to the fortress of Tyre and to all the towns of the Hivites and Canaanites. Finally they went to Beersheba in the south of Judah.
After they had gone through the whole land, they came back to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
Joab reported the number of people to the king. In Israel there were eight hundred thousand strong men who could fight with a sword, and in Judah there were five hundred thousand.

After David had counted the people, his heart troubled him. David said to the LORD, "I have sinned greatly by what I have done. Now, LORD, I beg you, take away the guilt of your servant. I have done a very foolish thing."
Before David got up the next morning, the LORD's message came to the prophet Gad, David's seer:
"Go and tell David, 'This is what the LORD says: I am giving you three choices. Choose one of them, and I will do it to you.'"

So Gad went to David and said to him, "Should there be seven years of famine in your land? Or should you run away from your enemies for three months while they chase you? Or should there be three days of deadly disease in your land? Think about it now and decide what answer I should give to the one who sent me."
David said to Gad, "I am in a terrible situation. Let us fall into the hands of the LORD, because his mercy is great. But do not let me fall into human hands."
So the LORD sent a deadly disease on Israel from that morning until the time he had set. Seventy thousand people died, from Dan to Beersheba.

When the angel reached out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the LORD felt sorry about the disaster. He said to the angel who was killing the people, "That is enough! Put your hand down." The LORD's angel was then at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

When David saw the angel who was striking down the people, he said to the LORD, "I am the one who has sinned and done wrong. These people are like sheep. What have they done? Please punish me and my family instead."
That day Gad came to David and said to him, "Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite."
So David went up, as Gad told him and as the LORD commanded.
Araunah looked out and saw the king and his officials coming toward him. So he went out and bowed down in front of the king with his face to the ground.

Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to see his servant?" David answered, "To buy your threshing floor, so that I can build an altar to the LORD and stop the disease that is killing the people."
Araunah said to David, "My lord the king, take whatever you want and offer it. Here are oxen for the burnt offering, and here are the threshing boards and the oxen's yokes to use for wood.
My king, I, Araunah, give all this to the king." And Araunah said to the king, "May the LORD your God accept your offering."

But the king said to Araunah, "No, I will pay you for it. I will not offer burnt offerings to the LORD my God that cost me nothing." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver, about six hundred grams.
David built an altar to the LORD there and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then the LORD answered his prayer for the land, and the disease stopped killing the people of Israel.
